title: Living in the District We're Buying
author: Đặng Minh
dek: A walk along the Ghềnh Ráng ridge at the hour the construction crews start, from the coast road to the three parcels we hold above it.
quote: We underwrite the district on a spreadsheet and then we live in it for two years. The two views disagree often enough to be worth the rent.

cover.caption: Ghềnh Ráng ridge, 06:40, looking north over the coast road.
cover.alt: Hillside road above Quy Nhơn bay at dawn, scaffolding on the slope below.

title: The Airport Road, Six Months On
dek: The Phù Cát link opened in January. We drove it at 07:00 and again at 18:00 to see what the 40-minute transfer time did to the parcels either side of it.
quote: Travel time fell as promised. Land within two kilometres of the interchange repriced first, and the frontage plots have yet to follow.

cover.caption: Phù Cát interchange to the northern beach strip, evening peak.
cover.alt: Dashboard view of the new airport road running between rice fields.

title: Fish Market Economics at 5am
dek: Fourteen frames from the Hàm Tử landing: who sets the price, who takes the ice, and why the restaurant supply chain we depend on begins three hours before the hotels open.

cover.caption: Hàm Tử landing, 05:10. First auction of the morning catch.
cover.alt: Traders sorting crates of fish under work lights on a concrete quay before sunrise.

title: Vietnam Coastal Macro Report 2026
dek: Capital flows out of the constrained primary markets and into coastal secondary cities: FDI registrations, land-use approvals and domestic wealth formation, 2019–2026.
quote: Vietnam's coastal secondary cities are absorbing institutional capital that the primary markets can no longer place, on infrastructure delivery rather than sentiment.

title: Vietnam Tail Risk Analysis
dek: The four exposures we model against a Vietnam coastal position — credit tightening, currency, typhoon frequency, and single-buyer tourism concentration — and what each costs at the fifth percentile.
quote: The binding constraint is not demand but the developer credit channel; every scenario we run degrades through it first.

title: Post-Pandemic Hospitality Yield Shifts
dek: Operating data from eleven coastal estates: how ADR, occupancy and staffing cost per key moved between 2019 and 2025, and where low-density stock now sits against hotel product.
quote: Low-density estates hold rate through the shoulder season; the volume-led hotel format recovers occupancy first and rate last.
